 No. 8 Tennessee Basketball vs. Radford: How to Watch, Betting Odds, Prediction, Full Preview
 By 
 Ryan Sylvia 
 - 
 Nov 9, 2026 
 KNOXVILLE, TN – November 03, 2026 – Forward DeWayne Brown II #6 of the Tennessee Volunteers during the game between the Wofford Terriers and the Tennessee Volunteers at Food City Center in Knoxville, TN. Photo By Andrew Ferguson/Tennessee Athletics 
 Tennessee basketball opened its season with a commanding win over Wofford last week and is now turning the page to its next challenge. On Monday night, the Vols will host Radford.
 Here’s what you need to know before the game.
 More From RTI:  Tennessee Basketball In Final Three For Blue Chip Center Recruit’s Imminent Commitment

 Start Time: 7 p.m. ET
 Location: Food City Center (Knoxville, Tennessee)
 Watch: SECN+
 Announcers: PxP – Myan Patel, Analyst – Steve Hamer, Reporter – Sarah Detwiler

 What Rick Barnes Said
 On if the win vs. Wofford was the first time he was able to show the team what it’s supposed to look like with the things he’s been harping on 
 “Against outside competition. We’ve done some. We’ve played really hard against each other in practice, but against outside competition, no question. We got some things on there that shows what we like, how we want to play. And these guys need it. They need to see it because we always talk about what we expect with our program, but they’ve never lived it. You know, they’ve never lived it. It’s all new to them. We’ve got 13 new guys.
 “Regardless of what outside people thought about how we’re going to play against Xavier, Duke, whatever. If we had our preference, we would have probably scrimmaged Davidson earlier because they would have exposed us drastically, as they always do. But it didn’t work out like that. I think the good Lord has it all (planned out). What happened at Duke, I won’t let them — I said it to them tonight. I said, the last time people saw us play, that’s who we were. And tonight you’ve got a chance to change that narrative. Because who we were at Duke, they beat us any and every way, and we helped them. We certainly helped them.
 “But I said, we’ve got to decide who this team is going to be. I thought, again, the second half, got more to it. I do think our depth had a conditioning factor at the end of the game, but if you go back to all of our teams, we’ve always been able to do that when we’ve been really good.”
 Prediction
 Tennessee looked like a much better team in its season-opening win against Wofford, and I’d expect that version of the Vols to be on display again. DeWayne Brown II may not go for 17 and 17 again, but he has the chance to build on his great start, as well. If he can live in double-double territory in these games, that’d obviously be a fantastic sign of what he’ll bring to the table throughout the year. I also expect Juke Harris to get going, at least scoring in double digits for the first time as a Vol.
 Tennessee 86, Radford 60
